The thesis is squarely on your patch. Litt argues the app is the wrong unit of personal software, because an app is someone else's one thing while real tasks are too idiosyncratic for that; the document becomes the medium instead. He traces it through Margin Notes, Embark, and now Notion, where agents embed interactive HTML into ordinary docs.

Two things worth your attention. His **quiz-before-merge rule** — he won't merge AI-generated code until he passes a quiz appended to the explainer — is a direct answer to rubber-stamping agent output. And his closing line that if the AI does it for you and you don't know how, you haven't gained the ability to build with it, sits right against the Vicky Zhao abstraction argument you captured earlier.
